This relationship is supported by the indirect pathway through Decitabine and Ivosidenib, both of which are indicated for the same condition. The evidence suggests that Enasidenib may exert its therapeutic effect by targeting the underlying molecular pathway associated with TRAML, though the exact mechanism of action remains to be fully elucidated. The presence of multiple indirect pathways linking Enasidenib to TRAML highlights the complexity of the relationship, but the consistent indication for the same condition across different drugs points to a shared biological context. The integration of these pathways underscores the importance of considering the broader therapeutic landscape when evaluating the potential reutilization of Enasidenib for TRAML.
